en.t: Was I really that excited just now?
Not quite that much, but a little...
It is all right for you to say that,
I really was unusually excited just now.

units.source_text: 一提到财产的事，我就会兴奋，

en.t: Whenever property comes up, I get excited,

units.source_text: 我不知道你是怎么看我的。

en.t: I do not know how you see me.
I am an extremely stubborn man,

units.source_text: 对于别人给我造成的屈辱与伤害，

en.t: As for the humiliation and harm others have caused me,

units.source_text: 无论是十年，还是二十年，都是忘不了的。”

en.t: whether ten years pass or twenty, I can never forget them.

units.source_text: 先生说这些话时比刚才更兴奋了。

en.t: As Sensei said these words, he grew even more excited than before.

units.source_text: 但是，令我感到惊讶的绝不是他说话的语气，

en.t: But what surprised me was by no means the tone of his voice,

units.source_text: 而是先生对我这么直言不讳本身的意义。

en.t: but the meaning of Sensei's very frankness toward me.

units.source_text: 从先生嘴里听到这样的坦白，是我无论如何也无法想象的。

en.t: Hearing such a confession from Sensei's own mouth was something I could never have imagined.

units.source_text: 先生的性格竟如此执着，这是我未曾想到的。

en.t: That Sensei's character was so tenacious was something I had never expected.

units.source_text: 我一直以为先生是个更为懦弱的人，

en.t: I had always thought Sensei was a weaker sort of person,

units.source_text: 而且，我已把我的崇拜之根扎在他那软弱而崇高之处了。

en.t: and I had already set the roots of my admiration in that weakness and nobility of his.

units.source_text: 由于一时气恼，想刺激一下先生的我，在先生的这番话面前变得渺小了。

en.t: I, who had meant in a moment of irritation to provoke Sensei a little, felt small before these words of his.
